# synology_nfs (Resource)

NFS service configuration. Export permissions are separate and are not implicitly changed by enabling the service.

## Adopt existing settings

1. Add the import block below with your resource address and the ID of the existing DSM object.
2. Set your arguments to the values DSM currently reports. The sample configuration shows the shape and uses example values.
3. Run `terraform plan`. For one import, apply only when it reports `1 to import, 0 to add, 0 to change, 0 to destroy`.

```terraform
import {
  to = synology_nfs.main
  id = "nfs"
}
```

## Example configuration

```terraform
resource "synology_nfs" "main" {
  enabled = false
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `enabled` (Boolean) Enable NFS.
- `nfs4_domain` (String) NFSv4 identity domain.
- `nfs4_enabled` (Boolean) Enable NFS version 4.
- `read_size` (Number) DSM read packet size.
- `write_size` (Number) DSM write packet size.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Singleton identity and import identifier: nfs. Destroy only releases Terraform management; it never resets DSM settings.
